questions.question: What planetary movement directly causes the cycle of day and night on Earth?

options.text: The Earth's rotation on its own axis

questions.explanation: As Earth spins, half the planet faces the Sun (day) while the other half faces away (night).

questions.question: Due to Earth's motion, in which direction does the Sun appear to rise?
questions.explanation: Because Earth rotates West to East, celestial bodies appear to rise in the East.

questions.question: Approximately how long does the Earth take to complete one full rotation on its axis?
questions.explanation: One rotation defines our 24-hour day.

questions.question: What is the movement of the Earth around the Sun called?
questions.explanation: Travelling along its orbital path around a central star is termed revolution.

questions.question: How long does one complete revolution of the Earth around the Sun take?
questions.explanation: This orbital period defines the length of a calendar year, with leap years accounting for the extra 6 hours.

questions.question: Does the Moon produce its own light?
questions.explanation: The Moon is a dark, rocky satellite that is visible only because it reflects solar radiation.

questions.question: What do we call the changing, illuminated shapes of the Moon as seen from Earth over a month?
questions.explanation: As the Moon orbits Earth, our viewing angle of its sunlit half changes, creating phases.

questions.question: What astronomical event occurs during a solar eclipse?

options.text: The Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth, blocking sunlight

questions.explanation: The Moon casts its shadow onto the Earth, temporarily turning day into twilight.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to look directly at a solar eclipse with naked eyes?

options.text: The intense solar radiation can severely and permanently damage the retina
It is too dark to see

questions.explanation: The lack of visible light dilates pupils, allowing harmful UV rays to burn the eye.

questions.question: What force from the Moon heavily affects Earth's oceans?
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravitational pull creates bulges in the oceans, resulting in high and low tides.

questions.question: If the Earth rotates from west to east, why do the Sun and stars appear to move from east to west?

options.text: It is an optical illusion caused by our perspective on a rotating object, similar to looking out of a moving train

questions.explanation: Relative motion makes stationary background objects appear to move in the opposite direction.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of different seasons (Summer, Winter) on Earth?

options.text: Earth gets physically closer to and farther from the Sun
The ~23.5° tilt of Earth's axis causes varying angles and durations of sunlight as it revolves
The Sun changes its heat output

questions.explanation: The axial tilt dictates how direct the sunlight is, driving massive climate shifts.

questions.question: If it is bright daytime in India, what is it likely to be in the USA?
questions.explanation: Because they are on opposite sides of the globe, one hemisphere faces the sun while the other is in the planet's shadow.

questions.question: What exactly is a lunar eclipse?

options.text: When the Earth comes exactly between the Sun and the Moon, casting its massive shadow onto the Moon
When the Sun completely blocks the Moon
When a cloud covers the Moon

questions.explanation: This occurs only during a full moon when the orbital alignment is perfect.

questions.question: Why don't we experience a solar and lunar eclipse every single month?

options.text: The Moon's orbit is tilted relative to Earth's, so the three bodies don't perfectly align every month

questions.explanation: The 5-degree tilt means the Moon usually passes slightly above or below Earth's shadow.

questions.question: If you look at the stars tonight at 8:00 PM, at what time will they be in the exact same position tomorrow night?
questions.explanation: Because Earth moves roughly 1 degree in its orbit daily, stars appear to rise 4 minutes earlier.

questions.question: Why do different constellations (groups of stars) appear in the night sky over the course of a year?

options.text: The stars are moving around the Earth
As Earth revolves around the Sun, our night-side faces completely different parts of deep space

questions.explanation: Our orbital journey changes our vantage point of the galaxy month by month.

questions.question: During winter in the Northern Hemisphere, how many hours of sunlight does the North Pole receive during one full rotation?
questions.explanation: Because the pole is tilted severely away from the Sun, it remains in the planet's shadow constantly.

questions.question: How long does it take for the Moon to orbit the Earth once?
questions.explanation: This roughly month-long orbital period dictates the cycle of the lunar phases.

questions.question: What is an equinox?

options.text: When the Earth's axis is tilted neither toward nor away from the Sun, making day and night nearly equal everywhere (around March 21, Sep 23)
The longest day of the year

questions.explanation: The word literally means "equal night," marking the onset of spring and autumn.

questions.question: Why can the much smaller Moon completely block the massive Sun during a total solar eclipse?

options.text: The Moon is about 400 times smaller, but also 400 times closer to Earth than the Sun, making their apparent angular sizes in the sky almost identical
The Earth's atmosphere magnifies the Moon

questions.explanation: This perfect cosmic coincidence allows the Moon's disc to exactly cover the solar photosphere.

questions.question: Why are total solar eclipses only visible from a very narrow path on Earth, while lunar eclipses are visible from the entire night side?

options.text: The Moon's dark shadow (umbra) is very small and traces a narrow path, whereas the Earth's shadow is massive and envelops the whole Moon

questions.explanation: The geometry of the shadows dictates the viewing area; Earth's shadow dwarfs the Moon.

questions.question: Why do we always see the exact same side of the Moon from Earth, never its "dark side"?

options.text: The Moon does not rotate at all
The Moon is "tidally locked"; its rotation period on its axis perfectly matches its orbital period around Earth (27.3 days)

questions.explanation: Because it spins at the exact same rate it revolves, one hemisphere always faces us.

questions.question: A student claims that summer happens because Earth gets physically closer to the Sun in July. How does a scientist correct this?

options.text: No, Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January (perihelion); seasons are strictly caused by the 23.5° axial tilt
No, the Sun gets hotter in July

questions.explanation: Proximity to the sun has negligible effect compared to the directness of sunlight caused by the tilt.

questions.question: If Nandhini sees a specific constellation rising exactly at midnight on June 21, when will she see it rising at exactly midnight again?
questions.explanation: It takes exactly one year (365 days) for the Earth to return to the precise orbital position relative to distant stars.

questions.question: If the Earth's axis were completely straight (0° tilt) instead of tilted, what would happen to the global climate?

options.text: The seasons would be more extreme
There would be no seasons; weather and daylight hours would remain almost constant year-round at any given latitude

questions.explanation: Without axial tilt, the angle of solar incidence would never change, eliminating seasonal variation.

questions.question: When is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, and what is this astronomical event called?
questions.explanation: The solstice occurs when the North Pole achieves its maximum tilt directly toward the Sun.

questions.question: The 4-minute daily shift in star rising times adds up to exactly how much time over one full year?
questions.explanation: 4 minutes × 365 days ≈ 1440 minutes, which equals 24 hours. Earth effectively completes one extra rotation relative to the stars during its orbit.

questions.question: Four friends watched a solar eclipse. Jyothi used a pinhole mirror projection, Ravikiran used certified solar goggles, Aruna went to a planetarium, and Adithya looked directly at it. Who was careless?
questions.explanation: Looking directly at the Sun during a partial eclipse bypasses the blink reflex, allowing intense UV rays to permanently burn the macula.

questions.question: How do spring tides (the absolute highest and lowest tides) relate to the phases of the moon?

options.text: They occur during full and new moons when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in a straight line, combining their gravitational pulls
They only happen in the spring season

questions.explanation: The vector addition of the Sun and Moon's gravity creates maximum tidal bulges during syzygy.
